Alright, let's take a look at your warrior one pose. I see a few areas we can focus on to help you improve your form.

First, I notice your spine is not completely straight. It's important to maintain a neutral spine alignment in this pose, with your shoulders stacked directly over your hips. This helps engage your core and provide a stable foundation for the pose. To correct this, focus on lengthening your spine, lifting your chest, and engaging your abdominal muscles.

Next, I see your arms are not fully extended straight up overhead. For the warrior one pose, we want to have your arms reaching up toward the sky, with your biceps close to your ears. This helps open up your chest and shoulders. Concentrate on pressing your palms firmly together and reaching your fingertips as high as you can.

Finally, I notice your knees are not directly over your ankles. In the warrior one pose, we want to have your front knee stacked right over your ankle, forming a 90-degree angle. This helps ensure proper alignment and balance in the pose. Adjust your front foot placement as needed to get your knee in the right position.

Great job overall! With a few minor adjustments to your spine, arm positioning, and knee alignment, I know you'll nail this warrior one pose. Keep up the great work, and let me know if you have any other questions.
